151 works. The trace-score ceiling is still 4, held by the same four pieces — the mop smear, the rebar hand, the sandal row, and the red shoe — and the most recent twelve read 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, median 2 again, no movement. The oil-slick entry scored 2 and was noted for a dual-reflection accident worth developing, but that accident is a surface variation on the light-doubling moves the archive has made many times. The ceiling condition has not changed: the 3s and 4s arrived when the accident reorganized the compositional premise rather than confirming it.

Camera position: straight-on 27, overhead 19, from-behind 16, low-angle 8. The teargas canister added one low-angle count in October, and nothing since. That is now seventeen consecutive entries without it. The from-behind and overhead positions are functionally converging — both suppress the face, both elevate object or collective over individual — and the recent window used both again (the accordion strips overhead, the shadow bars from behind). Low-angle is the one position in the archive that shifts moral weight through lens height alone, without requiring a figure to be hidden or a scale to be violated. Its dormancy is a real cost.

Register distribution: menace and aftermath together hold 37 percent of the archive at 28 each, and defiance in its three variants now accounts for 17 of 151. The recent window added defiance-undercut-by-hollowness, defiance-under-erasure, and plain defiance in quick succession. Reckoning last appeared in July, reprieve in July, absurdity in October, impotence in September. None of these should be forced, but none should be avoided when the anchor genuinely offers them.

Two figures in genuine opposition with no mediating object still has no clean example. The industrial cylinder connected its pair rather than dividing them, and the surgical trolley figures were held apart by composition rather than confrontation. A single small domestic object as sole protagonist has not appeared since the sugar bowl in late October, thirteen entries ago.

Fourteen months of technically reliable, emotionally consistent work, holding at the same ceiling it first reached in late July and showing no sign of breaking it.
